153	  **post-merge conversation capture** (`node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue
154	  <n>`, the "After the merge" section of `merge-to-main`). So: before merging in a dual-repo
155	  session, resolve the merge skill **by target repo**, not by which skill matched first — and
156	  treat capture as part of the merge, not as an optional epilogue.
157	- **Fail-soft SessionStart steps hide their own breakage fleet-wide — test the emitted
158	  output, not the exit code.** Every `engine/pack_loader/` SessionStart step
159	  (`inject-pack-prose.mjs`, `mount-skills.mjs`, `env-requirements.mjs`) wraps its body in
160	  `try { ... } catch {}` so a broken loader never blocks a session. That fail-soft is deliberate,
161	  but it means a runtime fault — a wrong dynamic-import target, a renamed module — exits 0 and
162	  simply emits nothing: no error, no signal. And because the engine is vendored verbatim into
163	  every member, one canon regression silently disables that step across the whole fleet at once.
164	  So a step like this must be guarded by a regression test that runs the real script against a
165	  real corpus and asserts the **positive** effect — prose IS emitted — never merely that
166	  `status === 0` (which fail-soft makes meaningless); see
167	  `engine-tests/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.test.mjs`.
168	- **The nightly self-refresh cannot repair the vendor-set computation — pin operational
169	  files against the REAL canon tree.** Baselining's converge re-runs
170	  `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs` from canon HEAD, so a bug *in that computation* is
171	  the one class of canon regression that is not self-healing: every refresh faithfully
172	  reproduces it, and recovery is an out-of-band vendor refresh applied to each member by
173	  hand. So when the vendor set excludes by *pattern*, an operational file that matches
174	  needs a by-path whitelist (`VENDORED_ENGINE_DOCS`) **and** a regression test asserting
175	  against the real canon tree, not only a synthetic fixture: a fixture keeps proving the
176	  whitelist mechanism works while the live path silently drops out from under it (see the
177	  paired tests in `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.test.mjs`).
178	- **A check that selects its inputs by path pattern can reach zero files and still pass — assert
179	  the live in-scope count.** When skills moved inside their owning pack (#385),
180	  `skill-no-enforcement-narration` kept scanning the root-level `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` layout: it
181	  matched nothing in any tree, read as live, and caught nothing until a human noticed the prose it
182	  should have flagged (#560 — 21 skills in scope once repointed). Its fixtures are why it hid so
183	  well; they spelled the same dead layout, so five green tests proved the *matching* and never the
184	  *selection*. A scan-based check therefore needs one assertion over the **real** tree that its
185	  scope is non-empty. Other half of the same class: agent-facing text pointing where the code isn't
186	  — the same PR fixed a rule whose `why`, fix text and `doc` all named `engine/checks_helpers` or
187	  `checks/lib`, neither of which ever existed. Nothing catches that on its own —
188	  `reference-integrity` is work-scoped and flags only paths the branch itself deletes — so grep the
189	  tree for any directory you name in a finding, a remedy, or a doc pointer before shipping it.
190	- **A scheduled task's precondition gates on movement in the window, never on standing state.** "An
191	  open PR exists" is true forever once it is true once, so the task wakes every night, spends an
192	  agent, and re-derives yesterday's verdict over an unchanged set (three of tidy-repo's tasks
193	  shipped that way; fixed in #554). Gate on the objects' own movement — a `touched` list or a
194	  tip-commit date, which the signal collector has to actually carry (`branches` carried names only,
195	  so "is any of this new" had no answer at all). A signal that is true most days on an active repo
196	  — a substantive `main` move — may only **widen** an already-triggered run, never wake one. And the
197	  gate is not the scope: where a verdict is relative to the rest of the set (superseded-by,
198	  already-in-`main`), newness gates and the full set stays the scope. (Portable — a promote
199	  candidate for `basics/scheduled-tasks.md`, which states the precondition contract but not this.)
200	- **You cannot force a due slot by running the scheduler workflow by hand.** Dueness is
201	  stateless — a slot is due iff its time falls in `(last successful run, now]` — so a
202	  `workflow_dispatch` run outside the slot's window succeeds, prints `- no tasks due`, and
203	  does nothing. It looks like a healthy run. To exercise a task Action-side, invoke its
204	  worker directly, or move the slot hour in `taskScheduler` and wait for the cron.
205	- **A scheduled task is gated twice — prove a change through `planRun`, never through its own
206	  precondition.** `planRun` computes the due list *before* any precondition runs, so a task whose
207	  most-recent slot has already been run is never evaluated and never reads its signals at all. #513's
208	  forced-run override landed with every test driving the precondition (or the signal collector) directly
209	  and was inert on exactly the run it existed for — the mid-day manual trigger — because the due-list
210	  gate it never touched had already dropped the task (`evaluations: []`; fixed in #516). A test that
211	  starts *inside* the gate proves only "works once evaluated" and says nothing about whether the task
212	  ever gets there. Drive the real `planRun` from a deliberately **non-due** slot: that is the only shape
213	  that catches it.
214	- **Every due task in a run shares ONE checkout — an agentless worker must not touch it.** The
215	  scheduler runs the whole due list in a single working tree, so a worker that checks out a branch or
216	  leaves an index behind hands the next task a tree it did not expect, and a run that dies leaves the
217	  mess for whatever follows. A task whose output is a regenerated file lands it through
218	  `engine/scheduler/deliver-generated.mjs` — git plumbing against the fetched base tip, with HEAD, the
219	  index and the working tree untouched — and reads its prior state from that base rather than local
220	  HEAD, so stacked runs stay idempotent. (`basics/baselining`'s own deliver is the deliberate
221	  exception: it commits a whole working tree and re-cuts a dated family branch; the landing itself —
222	  delivery preference, CI dispatch, arm/land/merge — is shared, in `engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs`.)
223	- **A code-search hit is evidence; a code-search miss is not — survey by reading each file.**
224	- **Derive the test file list from the tree — every hand-written glob here under-runs the suite.**
225	  There is no `package.json` and no test script, so each session invents its own incantation and
226	  silently verifies less than it thinks. Measured in this checkout: `node --test <dir>` does not
227	  recurse — it resolves the path as a module and dies with `Cannot find module`; bash `**` is not
228	  recursive without `globstar`, so `engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs` reaches
229	  **37 of 65** tracked test files. Four consecutive sessions (2026-07-26, #459/#452/#435/#468) each
230	  wrote a different command and reported 587, 690, 621 and 697 tests — three of them pushed after
231	  running a strict subset. Neither published list is authoritative either: `ci.yml`'s `tests=(…)`
232	  array omits `vendoring/*.test.mjs`, and `engine/checks/README.md`'s "as CI runs it" one-liner
233	  names `engine/test/`, `skills/` and `mount/`, none of which exist. So enumerate from git and let
234	  the count speak: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. (The drift-guard, once the array is
235	  clean: assert every tracked `*.test.mjs` is matched by `ci.yml`'s globs.)
236	- **A branch that waited overnight has lost its base *and* possibly its premise — re-verify the
237	  problem still exists on current `main`, unasked.** This repo merges its own scheduled-task PRs
238	  without a human, on top of multi-phase migrations that retire whole directories: measured on
239	  PR #465, `main` moved **14 commits in 13.7 hours** and one of them (#473, "retire `run_daily/`")
240	  *deleted the file the PR's diagnosis rested on* and had already landed most of its content. The
241	  branch rebased cleanly and the tests stayed green — the change was simply no longer the change to
242	  make, and the correct move was `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` and re-applying only the
243	  surviving slice (9 files → 2). So syncing the base is not the check; the check is a **content**
244	  one: after `git fetch`, read what the new commits did to the surface you are changing and state
245	  whether the problem is still there, what the goal was, and what survives. Do this whenever you
246	  return to a paused branch, before presenting it — the owner should never have to ask "is this
247	  change still needed" (asked three times on #465 before it was volunteered).
248	- **Every `Claude_Code_Remote` call costs minutes, and a call that returns nothing has NOT failed —
249	  never re-issue it.** The whole server behaves this way, not one tool: measured over four sessions
250	  on 2026-07-29, `add_repo` ran 270–285s a call, `send_later` 117–390s, `list_triggers` 139–325s,
251	  `delete_trigger` 286–301s, `subscribe_pr_activity` 14–237s. They read like cheap registrations,
252	  so a session issues one, sits through minutes of silence, concludes it hung, and issues it again —
253	  and *the duplicate is the dominant cost*, because the first call had already succeeded:
254	  **#562 (`2026-07-29T1500Z`) — 6 `add_repo` calls, 1121s of that session's 1391s of tool
255	  wall-clock (81%)**, with `HelloWorldFlutterApp` added twice (285s + 271s); **#553
256	  (`2026-07-29T2206Z`) — the same PR check-in `send_later`d 4 times, 1107s of 2028s (55%)**; **#544
257	  (`2026-07-29T1248Z`) — `list_triggers` ×2, `delete_trigger` ×2 on one trigger id, `send_later` ×2:
258	  1854s of 2472s (75%)**, in a session whose real work was 166 tool calls. `AskUserQuestion` shares
259	  the shape — #559's session asked one question twice for 218s + 204s. So: **one call per intent,
260	  ever**, and when what you want is "is it green yet", read the check status directly and merge on
261	  the already-green result rather than buying a notification. Budget these calls before making them:
262	  four of them is most of an hour.
263	- **Sync local `main` with `git reset --hard origin/main`, never `git pull` — this repo's session
264	  clones are shallow.** The post-merge sync step of `merge-to-main` is where it bites, and it bit
265	  five separate sessions on 2026-07-29 alone (#548, #551, #537, #559 and the session-end capture of
266	  `73a4db48`). A shallow clone has no common ancestor with the fetched remote, so `git pull` either
267	  demands an explicit strategy or reports the stale local ref as carrying unique commits it does not
268	  have — and the tempting reading, "local `main` has work the remote lacks", is wrong every time:
269	  the session's own work is already *in* `origin/main`, which is why it just merged. #537's session
270	  spent 87s across `git pull`, `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` and log comparisons proving
271	  that from scratch; #559's landed on "git sees no common ancestor" the same way. Nothing of value
272	  is ever on this repo's local `main`, so the sync is unconditional: `git fetch origin main && git
273	  reset --hard origin/main`. (Portable — a promote candidate for `git-github`'s merge procedure,
274	  where "your clone may be shallow" is true of any container-hosted session.)
275	- **The home has no `.claudinite/shared/` mount — machinery paths must accept both roots.** A
276	  consumer runs the vendored engine under `.claudinite/shared/engine/…` with packs under
277	  `.claudinite/(shared|local)/packs/…`; the home *is* the corpus and runs the same code from the
278	  repo root. So a path, regex, or workflow command written to the consumer mount shape works
279	  fleet-wide and fails on exactly this repo — the last place anyone exercises it, so the break
280	  surfaces late. Write the two-root form up front: make the `.claudinite/(shared|local)/` prefix
281	  optional in a pattern, and in a command probe for `.claudinite/shared/` first, falling back to
282	  the repo root.
283	- **Tightening a contract that member-owned files must satisfy has NO carrier — baseline
284	  migrations move paths, not schemas — so it lands as a fleet-wide silent break.** Vendoring
285	  refreshes `.claudinite/shared/` only; a member's `.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/pack.mjs` is
286	  the member's own content, which no converge may edit. And `migrations/` cannot help: its record
287	  is a path relocation (`aliases: [{ canonical, legacy }]`, applied by `applyFileAliases`), so it
288	  has no way to express "the field `rules` is now `worldRules`/`workRules`" or "`ruleRoutingGuidance`
289	  is now required" — exactly what #555 tightened, shipping no record because there was none to
290	  ship. The break is worse than loud: `normalizeManifest` returns `{ ...mod, rules }` with `rules`
291	  rebuilt **only** from the two scoped keys, so a legacy manifest's array is overwritten with `[]`
292	  and **that pack's checks simply stop running** — no error, the pack still loads. Measured on
293	  2026-07-30: **eleven local packs across ten of the thirteen members** had to be rewritten by
294	  hand in one session, and the members' own pack tests asserted `pack.rules` and went red on CI
295	  the moment the manifests moved. So before tightening anything a member's own file must satisfy,
296	  ask what carries it across the fleet; if the answer is "nothing", the change is not ready —
297	  accept the legacy shape in `normalizeManifest` (and say so) until a carrier exists, and never
298	  let a stale declaration degrade to *fewer checks running* rather than a failure.
299	- **A migration record is always the newest code; the engine that executes its result is the
300	  member's, and only as new as its last successful converge.** `migrations/apply.mjs` runs from a
301	  **fresh canon clone**, so every member gets today's record — but the worker that then commits and
302	  pushes it is the member's own **vendored** `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs`,
303	  frozen at whatever converge last succeeded. So a record that needs a *new engine capability* to be
304	  deliverable is a **deadlock** on any member that hasn't got it yet: the record fires, the converge
305	  fails, the mount never advances — and the engine fix that would make the record deliverable can
306	  never arrive, because the only thing that could carry it is the converge the record is breaking.
307	  Measured 2026-08-05: `sheepdog-fleet-baseline` materialized `.github/workflows/fleet-baseline.yml`,
308	  which the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` may not push, and wedged `missingbulb/Sheepdog`'s every converge
309	  **twice** — the second time *after* the engine fix (#651) had merged to canon, because Sheepdog was
310	  still running the pre-fix worker. So when a record depends on engine behaviour newer than the record's
311	  own landing date, make `appliesTo` **probe the member's own mount** for that capability and stay
312	  inert until it reads back — self-healing in two cycles, no manual step on any member (#652). Probe by
313	  content, not by version: the baselining stamp covers the whole mount and says nothing about *which*
314	  engine change is in it. And fail **safe** — an unreadable or missing mount file must read as "not
315	  capable", which only ever delays that one record instead of wedging the repo.
316	- **When the owner asks why something failed, lead with the throwing call site — `file:line`, the
317	  function, and which side enforced it.** He is asking for the mechanism, not the sequence; an answer
318	  that narrates the flow correctly but never names the line reads as unanswered, and he will ask again.
319	  Measured 2026-08-05 (#649): "explain why the flow failed" → a correct stage-by-stage narrative →
320	  *"You didn't explain my question from before. What exactly threw the error?"* → `worker.mjs:429`,
321	  `execFileSync` on `git push`, refused **remote-side** on receipt → understood immediately. Three
322	  rounds and ~10 minutes for one fact that fits on one line. The local/remote half matters as much as
323	  the line: it is what says why nothing local — the commit, `migrations/apply.mjs`, the suite, the
324	  sweep — saw it coming.
325	- **This repo's fleet machinery reports success from reaching the end of the code path, not from
326	  the artifact — check the response, and alarm on the stamp.** `deliver()` in
327	  `packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs` destructured only `json` from the PR-open POST and
328	  never read `status`, so a 403 (the member's *"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull
329	  requests"* setting, invisible from inside the Action) put the error body in `pr`, left
330	  `pr.node_id` undefined, skipped the auto-merge arm silently — and the run still logged
331	  `preprocessing basics/baselining: ok`. It compounds because `openMaintenancePull` reuses by open
332	  **PR**, not by branch: a cycle that pushes a branch but fails to open its PR finds nothing to
333	  reuse and mints a fresh one nightly. Measured 2026-07-29/30: **eleven of twelve consumers frozen
334	  on the 2026-07-28 canon ref, 27 orphan `claudinite/maintenance-*` branches, several repos
335	  carrying two for one day** — and every nightly run green throughout. Nothing detected it; the
336	  owner did, by feel ("I feel the situation is bad"). Two habits follow. Read the status of every
337	  API write whose result you then branch on — a body-only destructure turns a refusal into a
338	  plausible object. And judge the fleet by **members' stamps**, never by scheduler run
339	  conclusions: the stamp is the only artifact that moves when baselining actually worked, which is
340	  why a stamp-staleness alarm (#331) is the missing guard and not a nice-to-have.
341	- **A fleet task's target list is enumerated dynamically; the routine's reachable-repo grant is
342	  hand-typed UI config — they drift, and the drift completes rather than fails.** The precondition
343	  builds its member list over `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` (`engine/scheduler/signals/fleet.mjs`, "the one
344	  token that can enumerate every repo the owner owns"), while the executor routine's MCP repo scope
345	  is set by hand in a UI no Action can read — so every member adopted from here on is enumerated by
346	  the precondition and invisible to the executor until someone widens the grant, and the gap only
347	  ever widens. Measured 2026-07-31 on #602: the dispatch named 12 members, the session's grant
348	  listed 10, and `growth-promote` reads members **over the API, never a checkout** — so the run
349	  would have noted two denials, proceeded, and filed a PR reading as a complete 12-member sweep.
350	  That is the worse of the two failure shapes: a routing mismatch stalls visibly (nothing happens,
351	  forever, and you notice), an unreachable target *succeeds wrongly*. So a fleet task must **fail
352	  loudly on a Context target it cannot reach** rather than proceed on a partial list, and adopting a
353	  member is not done until the routine's repo scope names it. No check can catch either half — this
354	  is routine config, not repo content.
355	- **`packs/README.md`'s check tally conflicts on every concurrent check-adding PR — recompute it,
356	  never take a side.** The hand-maintained "Hardcoded conformance checks" count is a repo-wide
357	  aggregate that each PR adding a rule must bump, so two such PRs in flight always collide there,
358	  and a branch that sat overnight collides with whatever landed meanwhile. Both sides of the
359	  conflict are stale the moment a third PR merges, so picking one — or incrementing the higher —
360	  is guessing; `packs-tests/catalog-tally.test.mjs` then goes red and the loop repeats. Derive it
361	  instead: discover the packs and count the active rules (`discoverPacks` +
362	  `run-active-pack-rules.mjs`), write that number, re-run the tally test. Measured 2026-07-31: the
363	  same tally was resolved three times in one day across two sessions (67→68 in #600, then 68→69→70
364	  twice inside #593's merge sequence).
365	  The nastier half of the same tally: a PR that **forgets** the aggregate doesn't conflict at all.
366	  #607 bumped its pack's own row in the catalog table — the *other* hand-maintained number a new
367	  rule must update — and never touched the corpus tally, so it merged clean on a suite that had run
368	  **once**, 12.5 hours earlier against a base that predated #606's own check, and left `main` red
369	  for every PR after it until #608 corrected 68 → 69 as an aside. A conflict at least stops you;
370	  the omission is silent, because a whole-tree aggregate is judged against the merged result and
371	  no branch's CI ever sees that. So a green from before `main` moved is not evidence about
372	  post-merge `main`: re-run the suite against current `main` immediately before merging a
373	  rule-adding PR, and update **both** numbers. (Portable — a promote candidate for `git-github`'s
374	  `merge-to-main`, which today says nothing about merging on a stale green.)
375	- **A worker whose cwd sits inside the tree it deletes takes every child with it — and the death
376	  arrives dressed as a legitimate outcome.** Baselining's prework runs with its cwd *inside the
377	  mount* (`.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/baselining/`), and converge step 2 `rmSync`s that
378	  whole tree before re-copying it. On Linux the worker survives on the unlinked inode and so does
379	  every child it spawns — so `check_the_world` died at `process.cwd()` with `ENOENT … uv_cwd`
380	  **before running a single check**, on every night that actually converged. Nothing looked wrong,
381	  because `escalation()` folded the crash into `checks-could-not-run` (worker.mjs:184) — a real code
382	  that reads as "this mount is too old to have checks". Net effect, fleet-wide and invisible: the
383	  conformance gate had never gated a converged tree, and every converging night burned an agent
384	  escalation on it. Caught live on a Sheepdog run, by nobody's test (#689/#691). Two habits. **Give
385	  every spawned child an explicit `cwd`** — `node([…], env, { cwd: root })` — rather than letting it
386	  inherit a directory its parent is about to delete, and resolve a root that cannot vanish underneath
387	  you (`--root`, then `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, then `cwd`: the order `check_the_world` and
388	  `engine/selftest.mjs` now share; the disagreement between them is the only reason selftest survived
389	  the same dead cwd untouched). And **when a crash and a benign state share one outcome code, the
390	  crash is unobservable** — keep "could not run" distinguishable from "had nothing to run".
391	- **When a member's maintenance PR won't land, read the member before theorizing — `unstable` beside
392	  a green sweep is a *parked* run, not a missing repo setting.** GitHub gates `pull_request` runs on
393	  Actions-pushed branches at `action_required`; a parked run never reports, so the PR reads
394	  `mergeable_state: unstable` and `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` refuses it. Measured 2026-08-07 (#676):
395	  a session read that signature as the members lacking *"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve
396	  pull requests"* and offered to have the owner flip it across the fleet. The owner's *"Check that
397	  setting. I think you're wrong."* was right, and the two reads that settled it took under a minute —
398	  each member's raw `.claudinite-checks.json` (all eight already said `delivery: auto-merge`) and the
399	  head sha's `pull_request` runs (4 of the last 5 parked `action_required`). The tree already knew:
400	  `baselining/worker.mjs` documents both shapes and the session quoted the wrong one — but this is a
401	  mistake of omission you make *without* opening that file, which is why it belongs here rather than
402	  beside the code. So propose a platform-settings change only as a **conclusion**, never as a
403	  diagnosis, and never on a symptom two API reads resolve. (Sibling of the standing ruling above that
404	  what Claudinite ships must run on the settings a member already has — that one is about what to
405	  *build*, this one about what to *believe*.)
406	- **A canon pack's directory name is kebab-case — lowercase words joined by single hyphens.** The
407	  directory name is the pack's public id: members spell it in `.claudinite-checks.json`, a migration's
408	  `declarePacks` op seeds it, the catalog row and every cross-reference repeat it — so a name in another
409	  casing is renamed later across all of them. Every pack under `packs/` follows it; `grow_with_claudinite`
410	  is the single grandfathered exception (it predates the convention and sits in every member's
411	  declaration, so renaming it would be a fleet migration, not a tidy-up). Nothing stated this until now,
412	  which is how `UserPreferencesStore` shipped in #567 and cost a whole-pack rename to
413	  `claude-code-web-users-support` after the owner asked for *"the appropriate casing for pack names"*.
414	  Name from the **surface** the pack serves, not the first feature you are building for it — that same
415	  rename widened the pack from one store to every Claude-Code-web capability. (Convertible: a check over
416	  `packs/*/pack.mjs` directory names would carry this whole rule, and the fixture is trivial — but any
417	  new rule moves `packs/README.md`'s check tally, which a growth-extract run may not touch. Left for the
418	  weekly prose-to-checks sweep's reviewed PR.)
419	- **The home is the last repo to receive its own stub changes — nothing delivers to it.** Every member
420	  gets `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml` written into `.github/workflows/` by its nightly
421	  converge; the canon has no mount and no converge, so its own copy is hand-maintained and drifts from the
422	  stub it ships. That drift is invisible until it is a permission denial in production: the canon's
423	  workflow sat on `actions: read` while the stub had carried `write` since store-release, so the CI
424	  dispatch POST 403'd and **only** the canon's own fold PR stranded — for ten days (#535, fixed in #704).
425	  Paired tests over the two files are not the safety net you think: one already asserted the
426	  `overrides` input on both and said nothing about `permissions`, so the drift walked straight past it.
427	  So when a change touches the vendored stub, edit the canon's `.github/workflows/` copy in the **same
428	  commit** and diff the two whole files, never just the lines you came for.
429

Migrations: one flat home, fetch-time relevance, no cleanup flows (#724)

Closes #725.

All migration records now live as equal, permanent folders directly under
migrations/ (<landed-date>-<slug>/migration.mjs). Relevance is decided at
fetch time: vendoring ships consumers only the records landed within the
last 7 days (recordDirIsRecent), migrationActive() tolerates by the same
window, and loadMigrations() loads everything present so a dormant project
baselining from a fresh canon clone applies the full history it missed.

Deleted the cleanup flows this replaces: fleet-apply/fleet-retire, the
canon-curation migrations-retire TTL archiver, the migrations-old/ archive,
retirableMigrations/migrationsPastTtl, and the retire/retireDeletesFromHome
record fields.

--- #541 assistant [13:25:59]
Comment class: feature

Yes, it makes sense — with three corrections, one of which I measured rather than argued.

**Size isn't enough, and this bug proves it.** I applied #274's correction to the Aug 7 catalogue — every start time an hour later, so every record's meaning changed — and the file moved by **0 bytes of 3,140,534**. A uniform correction is routinely byte-length-neutral. Size catches truncation, which the read guards in this PR already catch, and nothing else.

**A hash needs an anchor, and that anchor is a manifest.** A hash *inside* each file proves nothing: a stale copy carries a perfectly valid hash of itself. `availability.min.json` has carried `"v": 1` all along and it was no help. You need an expected hash from something fetched fresher than the thing you're checking — one small manifest of every asset and its hash, fetched uncached on every load. That's the one file that must never carry a TTL, or you've just moved the staleness up a level and hidden it better.

**Don't re-hash cached bodies — record the hash you stored.** Verifying by hashing means pushing 3MB through a digest on the critical path on every load, to answer a question the bookkeeping already knows. Store the manifest hash in the stamps map beside the entry and the check is a string compare.

The payoff is bigger than corruption detection, and it's the real argument for your idea: **a manifest

## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest

Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:

- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below

- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is

## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference

`.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:

- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm

- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
  materializing it is baselining's converge job, not yours.
- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the dispatch issue.

## 2. Arm auto-merge

Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands

- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
